records.label: Three Bedouin sibs

phenotypes.text: nail/phalangeal hypoplasia of fingers and toes
very low mitotic index of peripheral blood lymphocyte cultures

quotes: Dysmorphic features in three sibs with congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia type 1 are described. These findings include growth retardation/short stature, congenital ptosis, abnormal tarsal bones, metatarsal duplication/hypoplasia, nail/phalangeal hypoplasia of fingers and toes, Madelung deformity, syndactyly of toes, and hallux valgus.
The patients also showed a very low mitotic index of their peripheral blood lymphocyte cultures. Phenotypic heterogeneity was elicited amongst the three Bedouin sibs.

records.label: Consanguineous Middle-Eastern pedigree
records.segregation: identified by whole genome sequencing and segregation analysis
quotes: We used whole genome sequencing and segregation analysis to identify a homozygous T to A transversion (c.533T>A), predicted to lead to a p.L178Q missense substitution in C15ORF41, a gene of unknown function, in a consanguineous pedigree of Middle-Eastern origin.

records.label: Two SouthEast Asian pedigrees
quotes: Sequencing C15ORF41 in other CDAN1 mutation-negative congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I pedigrees identified a homozygous transition (c.281A>G), predicted to lead to a p.Y94C substitution, in two further pedigrees of SouthEast Asian origin.

notes.statement: Babbs et al. (2013) noted that no likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation is detected in approximately 20% of cases of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I, suggesting at least one other locus, and identified C15ORF41 as such a locus.
quotes: However, no likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation has been detected in approximately 20% of cases, suggesting the presence of at least one other locus.

notes.statement: Babbs et al. (2013) found that the haplotype surrounding the C15ORF41 c.281A>G mutation suggested a founder effect for this mutation in Pakistan.
quotes: The haplotype surrounding the c.281A>G change suggests a founder effect for this mutation in Pakistan.

notes.statement: Babbs et al. (2013) used detailed sequence similarity searches to predict that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease belonging to the Holliday junction resolvase family of proteins.
quotes: Detailed sequence similarity searches indicate that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease that is a member of the Holliday junction resolvase family of proteins.

notes.statement: Ahmed et al. (2006) used linkage and mutational analysis of the CDAN1 gene and found genetic heterogeneity in congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.
quotes: Linkage and mutational analysis of the CDAN1 gene reveals genetic heterogeneity in congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.

notes.statement: Ahmed et al. (2006) presented evidence of genetic heterogeneity in congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.
quotes: Evidence of genetic heterogeneity in congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia type I.

notes.statement: Sabry et al. (1997) concluded that their report confirmed the association between a subset of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type 1 and a specific form of distal limb anomalies. They suggested that congenital ptosis and a low mitotic index might also be part of the syndrome.
quotes: The present report confirms the association between a subset of congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia type 1 and a specific form of distal limb anomalies and suggests that other traits, congenital ptosis and low mitotic index, could represent part of the syndrome profile.
